title: Token-aware host coalescer and fused memcpy scheduler to lower CPU-GPU overhead
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Host-side overhead from many small memcpy operations and threadpool contention during prefill and decode paths is contributing to higher tail latency and reduced effective GPU utilization. Current observations show the host CPU spends significant cycles coalescing numerous tiny token buffers and scheduling many small GPU memcpy ops, amplified under multimodal and chat workloads with many short-turn requests.

Goal: Implement a token-aware host coalescer that aggregates small outgoing batches into fewer fused memcpy operations and a fused-memcpy scheduler that uses GPU queue depth and per-request token size heuristics for prioritized dispatch. Reduce CPU context switches and backlog on the threadpool while preserving latency SLOs for short requests.

Success metrics: reduce host CPU sys+user for serving by >=10% under mixed load; reduce memcpy syscall count by >=50%; improve p95 decode latency by >=7% on medium load profile; maintain or improve GPU token throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Host memcpy syscall count reduced by at least 50% in the synthetic mixed-short-turn workload compared to baseline (measurement harness linked)
End-to-end p95 decode latency improves by >=7% under the defined medium traffic profile without increasing p99 beyond noise
CPU utilization attributed to host pipeline (prefill+decode) decreases by >=10% on the test fleet during steady-state
Canary rollout completed to 10% of traffic with monitoring dashboards (latency, memcpy rate, GPU queue depth) and automatic rollback guardrails
Telemetry emitted: fused_memcpy_count, fused_memcpy_bytes, host_coalescer_backpressure, token_coalesced_rate (all as counters/gauges)
No regressions on model output correctness or ordering; existing tests for streaming and KV-cache preserved
implementation_notes: Design a host_coalescer component that groups outgoing token buffers by destination GPU/stream and time-window (configurable micro-window ~100-300us), using token_count thresholds (configurable) to decide fuse vs immediate dispatch.
Expose a lightweight backpressure signal derived from GPU submission queue depth + inflight memcpy bytes; coalescer should delay non-latency-sensitive batches when backpressure is high.
Implement fused memcpy using a scatter-gather buffer allocator to create contiguous DMA-friendly blobs to reduce the number of copy system calls; keep CPU-side copy to a single pass per fused blob.

Threadpool changes: introduce a two-level priority queue in the host pool: short-latency tasks (single-token/short-turn requests) get preemptive scheduling; coalescing and background memcpy flush tasks run at lower priority.
NUMA-awareness: when available, prefer coalescing and flush operations on the same NUMA node as the target GPU to reduce cross-node memcopy cost.
Kernel selection impact: add a hint to kernel picker that records coalesced batch sizes to help runtime choose kernels optimized for larger fused dispatches where appropriate.
Feature flagging path: feature can be toggled per-region and per-customer for canary; must be off by default in private deployments until vetted.
Testing: synthetic harness for small-turn chat workload, multi-tenant stress test with pinned GPUs, and unit tests that verify ordering and correctness across fused blobs
progress_updates: 2025-03-10: Spike completed — microbench shows ~35% reduction in memcpy syscall rate when fusing batches of up to 8 short-token buffers in a single thread. Prototype implemented in local dev branch.

2025-03-12: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decision: configurable time-window approach instead of fixed token-only threshold to better handle bursty arrival patterns. Agreed to track GPU queue depth metric for backpressure.
2025-03-14: Implemented initial fused memcpy allocator and integrated with host submission code path. Added metrics scaffolding for fused_memcpy_count and host_coalescer_backpressure.

2025-03-16: Load test on staging w/ mixed chat and long-seq jobs. Observed ~12% CPU reduction on host pipeline and p95 latency improvement ~6%. Some p99 tail variations correlated with long-coalesce windows — tuning needed.
2025-03-18: Tuned time-window from 300us -> 150us for latency-sensitive tenants; added priority queue in threadpool. Preparing canary PR and dashboards for runtime-1.20 release window.
